key_step: Cover-up values A_k as signed factorial products, then ratio cancellation.
justification: Routine chain of cover-up residues and factorial cancellation; numerical format means no options to check, but every step is standard. Closest anchor is 2026-P2-Q3 (L2, routine chain with careful finish).

key_step: Periodic integrand: [a] full periods of e-1 plus a partial period.
justification: One familiar periodicity move followed by a short equation to solve for {a}; options allow a check. Similar in demand to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, integral equation then evaluate) and above the pure one-trick L1 of 2021-P2-Q11.

key_step: Square the root sum to get ln(2+2sqrt(1-x^2)), then by parts and t-substitution.
justification: Four linked stages (evenness, log-square trick, by parts, substitution to an inverse-sine integral) with no shortcut and several places for a slip; the log-square idea is not a stock coaching pattern. Heavier than 2024-P2-Q16 (L2, king property) and comparable to 2021-P2-Q16 (L3).

key_step: [[x]-sin x]=[x]+[-sin x] and [t]+[-t]=-1 over a symmetric interval.
justification: Two familiar greatest-integer facts combined with the f(x)+f(-x) property; only a short chain. Same single-trick-with-routine-setup flavour as 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) plus an extra step, hence L2.

key_step: f(x)=asinh x is odd, so the sin f part integrates to zero.
justification: One parity observation after a cosine addition formula; the oddness of log(x+sqrt(x^2+1)) must be recognised. Three routine steps, no insight beyond parity, so above the one-move L1 of 2021-P2-Q11 and in line with 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

key_step: Recognise a Riemann sum and convert it to the integral of f(5x) on [0,1].
justification: A single standard recognition (limit of a sum to an integral) with a linear integrand. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q11 (L1, one direct integral).

key_step: Period pi reduces 100 periods to one; then integrate e^{-t} sin^2(pi t) by the standard exponential-trig formula.
justification: Two standard ideas (periodicity of a fractional-part integrand, exponential times cosine integral) chained with exact algebra and a final match to the given form; options help. Slightly heavier than 2023-P2-Q1 (L2) but without any non-routine idea.

key_step: King property with x -> pi/4 - x turns tan 2x into cot 2x; the two forms add to 1.
justification: Textbook king-property question where the reflection is easy to spot. Same as 2026-P2-Q4 (L1, king property on 1/(3^x+3)).

key_step: f(x)=integral of [y] is continuous with f'=[x] away from integers; one-sided derivatives differ at integers.
justification: Standard integral-function-of-greatest-integer question: compute (or use FTC), then check continuity and one-sided derivatives. Statements are coarse so options help. Easier than 2024-P2-Q13 (L3, piecewise g with zeros and right-derivative).

key_step: Split |1-t| at t=1 to get f(x) for x>2; compare values and one-sided derivatives at 2.
justification: Routine split of a modulus integral then a continuity/differentiability check at one point with all four options available. Comparable in kind to 2024-P2-Q13 (L3) but much shorter and with options, hence L2.
